chapter: First bands, illness and Houston life
title: Lesson learned: no tabs, pay as you go
summary: From the ice cream incident Cobb draws his rule against running tabs, which he enforced with his own sidemen on the road.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: And you know, from that incident, ...
But that was rather bad for him not to tell you it would be deducted from your check.

But I tell you what I learned from that. See, everything is a learning experience. See, you buy your experience. Or you buy whatever it is you know. Today, I don't run no tabs. In a bar where I'm playing, I pay as I go. If I'm working for a week out of town, I pay -- I don't want nobody to hold nothing till the weekend on me, because you know, they know I'll pay it.

"What I owe you?" I check out that night, and I tell my crew, and that was when I was on the road, you got one draw a during the night, the middle of the week, like Wednesday, I don't want no tabs; I want no extra bookkeeping; I don't want nothing. Pay as you go. And that was my policy when I had my band out, and I did it myself. I

didn't tell them to do something I didn't do, because it can become extra bookeeping. Everybody hears you got one, they're gonna run over, and at the end of the week, you got your payroll made out, then here you go, you got to change it around because here's some extra money coming in. It's too much.
But also, I mean it gives them an opportunity to pad more, like you just described.
I know they will pay it.
Yeah, but I mean on one night, you could pretty well remember what you had, couldn't you? But you can't remember a whole week, can you?
But get rid of it that night.
As you go along and you buy things, and you're having a ball the whole week, and you end up with everything you made, you owe it back. And I don't go for that. Really.
